_source: corpus_files/training/*Assessment*.txt — the objective questions as administered. No answer key and no per-question accuracy are asserted here; the reports name only the best- and least-answered topics.

district_baseline.text: What is the name of Andhra Pradesh's long-term development vision launched by CM Chandrababu Naidu?
options: Vision AP 2030
Swarna Andhra @2047
Sunrise Andhra Plan
Nava Andhra Mission 2050

district_baseline.text: Andhra Pradesh's Swarna Andhra @2047 vision aims to transform the state into a ₹308 lakh crore economy. What is this approximately in USD?
options: USD 500 billion
USD 1.2 trillion
USD 2.4 trillion
USD 4 trillion

district_baseline.text: The Swarna Andhra @2047 vision targets what per capita income for AP citizens by 2047 (currently ~₹2.66 lakh)?
Which of the following is NOT one of the core pillars of the Swarna Andhra @2047 Vision?
options: Zero Poverty and Inclusive Growth
Valley of Innovation and Speed of Business
Centralised Public Sector-led Industrial Growth
Tech-enabled Universal Healthcare

district_baseline.text: The Swarna Andhra @2047 KPI Portal monitors performance at which administrative levels?
options: State level only
District and state levels only
Mandal, district, constituency and state levels
Mandal and district levels only — state is monitored separately

district_baseline.text: The KPI framework under Swarna Andhra @2047 is primarily aligned with which global framework?
options: BRICS Sustainable Growth Indicators
UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
World Bank Human Capital Index
NITI Aayog's Aspirational Districts Programme

district_baseline.text: What annual growth rate does the Swarna Andhra @2047 vision document target for the AP economy?
options: 8% — in line with India's national average
10% — matching the fastest-growing large states
12% — as recommended by NITI Aayog
15% — to reach USD 2.4 trillion by 2047

district_baseline.text: As a district officer, what is your PRIMARY role in the Swarna Andhra KPI system?
options: Entering mandal-level data and forwarding it to the state without review
Entering, verifying and approving district/mandal level KPI achievement data
Setting district KPI targets independently based on local priorities
Reviewing KPI data only when a state-level audit is initiated

district_baseline.text: What is the correct relationship between GVA and GDP?
options: GDP = GVA + Total Government Expenditure
GDP = GVA + Net Taxes on Products (Taxes minus Subsidies)
GDP = GVA adjusted for inflation using the Price Deflator
GDP = GVA minus Depreciation of fixed assets

district_baseline.text: Which approach measures GDP by summing value added at each stage of production across all sectors?
options: Expenditure Approach — adds up all spending in the economy
Income Approach — sums wages, profits and rents
Production (Output) Approach — sums GVA across all sectors
Base Year Approach — fixes prices at a reference year

district_baseline.text: The 'bottom-up approach' to estimating District Domestic Product means:
options: National GDP is calculated first and then disaggregated to districts using population or area shares
Economic data is collected and aggregated upward from district and mandal level
Only the lowest-income sectors in a district are measured to set a baseline
District-level GVA is estimated using state-level averages applied uniformly

district_baseline.text: Which of the following economic activities belongs to the TERTIARY sector?
options: Aquaculture and prawn farming
Food processing in a registered factory
Wholesale and retail trade
Electricity generation from a thermal power plant
Total population of a district
Value added after deducting intermediate inputs from output
Total government expenditure
Total exports of a state
Output + Intermediate Consumption
Output − Intermediate Consumption
Taxes − Subsidies
Consumption + Investment

district_endline.text: Agriculture, livestock, forestry, fishing and mining are part of which broad sector?
options: Primary sector
Secondary sector
Tertiary sector
Financial sector

district_endline.text: At constant prices, estimates generally use
options: Current year production with current year prices
Base year production with current year prices
Current year production with base year prices or deflators
Only population data

district_endline.text: When direct district-level GVA data is not available, district estimates are usually prepared by
options: Ignoring the sector
Apportioning state estimates using suitable district indicators
Using only national averages
Taking equal share for all districts

district_endline.text: Which is a key limitation in estimating district domestic product?
options: Too much direct district data is available
Districts have identical economic structures
Many activities require proxy indicators or allocation keys
GVA is not sector-specific

district_endline.text: For district-level banking and insurance estimates, state GVA is apportioned using
options: Forest area
Tourist arrivals
Bank credits and deposits
Paddy production

district_endline.text: In Mandal Domestic Product allocation, production/output indicators are considered useful because they are
options: Closest to direct economic activity
Always available from Census
Unrelated to GVA
Used only for services sector

district_endline.text: Which of the following is the correct four-step economic engine cycle discussed in the presentation?
options: Plan - Spend - Report - Close
Identify - Understand - Strategise - Monitor
Survey - Budget - Approve - Audit
Collect - Compile - Publish - File

district_endline.text: How should a district identify its priority sectors for GVA growth?
options: Select only sectors with the highest population share
Compare district sector share with AP average and identify comparative advantage
Choose sectors randomly to ensure balance
Focus only on sectors that declined in the previous year

district_endline.text: Which indicator is most directly linked to manufacturing formalisation and MSME GVA improvement?
options: Number of tourist arrivals
Udyam registrations and industrial electricity consumption
Forest area and rural population
Bank deposits alone

district_endline.text: In the tourism and trade growth equation, GVA improves mainly through:
options: Number of tourists, spend per tourist and length of stay
Only the number of government employees
Only agricultural production
Only road length in the district

district_endline.text: Why should district officers monitor high-frequency proxy indicators instead of relying only on annual DDP publication?
options: Because annual DDP is enough for all operational decisions
Because monthly signals help identify gaps and correct course before year-end
Because proxy indicators are unrelated to GVA
Because monitoring should be avoided at district level

district_endline.text: For improving banking and insurance GVA, which set of variables should district officials review regularly?
options: Credit, deposits, CD ratio, bank branches and financial inclusion
number of tourist guides
crop area under paddy
number of government buildings

constituency.section: Improving GVA at constituency and mandal level
constituency.text: Which of the following is most directly linked to improving primary sector GVA?
options: Setting up agro-processing units for local produce
Increasing crop productivity, livestock output and irrigation efficiency
Developing rural tourism and hospitality facilities
Expanding market yards and financial service access

constituency.section: Improving GVA at constituency and mandal level
constituency.text: Value addition improves local GVA mainly because it:
options: Increases the economic value of raw produce through processing or branding
Increases cultivated area without changing production practices
Reduces the need for market linkage by focusing only on production
Shifts all agricultural workers into non-farm employment

constituency.section: Improving GVA at constituency and mandal level
constituency.text: Which intervention is most appropriate for improving secondary sector GVA?
options: Establishing food processing, packaging and manufacturing units
Promoting crop diversification and micro-irrigation
Developing tourism circuits and local hospitality services
Expanding access to banking and digital payments

constituency.section: Improving GVA at constituency and mandal level
constituency.text: Which of the following best represents a tertiary sector activity?
options: Milk production and poultry rearing
Mango cultivation and oil palm farming
Tourism, logistics, trade and financial services
Rice milling and cashew processing

constituency.section: Improving GVA at constituency and mandal level
constituency.text: The main purpose of analyzing sector-wise GVA contribution is to:
options: Identify key growth drivers and prioritize sector-specific interventions
Calculate only the total number of workers in each sector
Estimate only scheme-wise expenditure across departments
Compare population growth across mandals or blocks

constituency.section: Improving GVA at constituency and mandal level
constituency.text: Which is the most suitable outcome indicator for agriculture-led GVA improvement?
options: Number of farmer meetings conducted during the year
Number of agriculture-related circulars issued by departments
Increase in area under high-value crops and micro-irrigation
Number of officials trained on agriculture schemes

constituency.section: Improving GVA at constituency and mandal level
constituency.text: Post-harvest infrastructure contributes to higher GVA by:
options: Improving storage, grading, processing and price realization
Increasing the number of farmers registered under schemes
Expanding irrigation coverage for traditional crops
Reducing the need for private sector participation

constituency.section: Improving GVA at constituency and mandal level
constituency.text: Departmental convergence is important for improving local economic growth because:
options: GVA growth requires coordinated action across production, infrastructure, skills, finance and markets
Each department can independently achieve GVA growth without coordination
It mainly helps in preparing more detailed administrative reports
It ensures that only one department is responsible for all economic outcomes

constituency.section: Improving GVA at constituency and mandal level
constituency.text: A strong review and accountability system for GVA improvement should focus on:
options: Tracking meetings, expenditure and number of instructions issued
Tracking baseline, targets, progress, bottlenecks and corrective action
Tracking only physical assets created under different schemes
Tracking beneficiary coverage without linking it to economic outcomes

master.text: Which statement best explains Gross Value Added (GVA)?
options: Total expenditure by government in a district
Value of output after deducting intermediate consumption
Total tax collected from all sectors
Total exports minus imports

master.text: Why is the production approach important for district-level economic analysis?
options: It uses only population data
It directly links sector activity, output and input use with value added
It avoids the need for sector-wise data
It is used only for national income estimation

master.text: What is the main difference between GSDP and GDDP?
options: GSDP is for districts and GDDP is for the state
GSDP is state-level income, while GDDP is district-level income
GSDP includes only agriculture, while GDDP includes all sectors
GDDP is estimated quarterly, while GSDP is estimated monthly

master.text: Which of the following is a key caution while interpreting district estimates?
options: District estimates are always based on complete direct data
District estimates should be read with methodology, data source and validation trail
District estimates do not require revision
Proxy indicators are never used in district estimation

master.text: If output increases but input costs rise faster, what may happen to GVA?
options: GVA will always increase
GVA may decline or grow slowly
GVA becomes equal to taxes
GVA is not affected by input costs

master.text: When direct district-level data is unavailable, how is district sector GVA generally estimated?
options: By dividing state GVA equally among all districts
By using suitable district-level allocation keys or proxy indicators
By ignoring that sector in district estimates
By using only national population share

master.text: Which of the following is an example of a primary sector activity?
options: Banking
Construction
Fishing
Public administration

master.text: In Mandal Domestic Product estimation, what does a mandal's share of an indicator determine?
options: Its tax rate
Its share of allocated district GVA for that activity
Its population growth rate
Its administrative ranking only

master.text: Why do proxy indicators need validation?
options: Because they are always wrong
Because they may only indirectly represent actual economic activity
Because they replace all official statistics
Because they are used only for agriculture

master.text: What is the main administrative message of the presentation?
options: Data should stop at reporting
District officials should use economic data for diagnosis, prioritisation and follow-up action
GDDP estimates are not useful for planning
Only state-level officers can influence economic management
